result_semantic_payload.summary: Three of the four CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log via exact verbatim order_id match, corroborated by identical amounts: ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000 USDT, settlement 2024-06-01 wallet TXabc111 amount 20000 ok), ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000 USDT, settlement 2024-06-01 wallet TXdef222 amount 15000 ok), and ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500 USDT, settlement 2024-06-02 wallet TXghi333 amount 31500 ok). The fourth CRM order, ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000 USDT, status cancelled), has no corresponding settlement line and therefore remains unconfirmed. One settlement log entry must be kept strictly separate from the CRM orders: the 2024-06-02 line "settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok". Its order id ORD-72033 does not exist in the CRM table, and the README rule states that a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order. Although ORD-72033 is a one-character near-miss of ORD-70233 (72 vs 70), the amounts differ sharply (9999 vs 31500) and the wallets differ (TXjkl444 vs TXghi333), so no fuzzy or amount-based reconciliation is admissible; it must not be merged into, attributed to, or used to confirm ORD-70233. The delegation's stated 'windows' source scope was not materialised: the task exposes no platform scenario and no source scopes, and the only evidence is three plain text/CSV/log files with no Windows registry, event-log, prefetch or amcache artifacts, so no Windows account-usage or execution-trace conclusions are supported.

claim_candidates.text: The linkage criterion between CRM orders and the settlement log is an exact verbatim match on order_id, as stated in the task README ('Settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim').

CRM order ORD-70231 (buyer wangqiang, 20000 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line dated 2024-06-01 with wallet TXabc111, amount 20000, result ok; order_id matches verbatim and the amount agrees exactly.

CRM order ORD-70232 (buyer zhaolei, 15000 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line dated 2024-06-01 with wallet TXdef222, amount 15000, result ok; order_id matches verbatim and the amount agrees exactly.

CRM order ORD-70233 (buyer sunli, 31500 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line dated 2024-06-02 with wallet TXghi333, amount 31500, result ok; order_id matches verbatim and the amount agrees exactly.

The settlement log entry '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must stay separate from the CRM orders because order id ORD-72033 does not exist in the CRM table, and the README forbids treating such a settlement as the same order.

ORD-72033 should not be reconciled to ORD-70233 despite the one-character id similarity (72 vs 70): the settlement amount 9999 does not match the CRM amount 31500, the wallets differ (TXjkl444 vs TXghi333), and the README's verbatim-id rule excludes any fuzzy or amount-based matching.

CRM order ORD-70234 (buyer qianer, 8000 USDT, status cancelled) is the only CRM order with no corresponding settlement log line, so it is not confirmed by the payment processor; its cancelled status is consistent with the absence of a settlement.

Net result: 3 of 4 CRM orders are confirmed by the settlement log (ORD-70231, ORD-70232, ORD-70233), 1 CRM order is unconfirmed (ORD-70234), and 1 of 4 settlement lines (ORD-72033) is unattributable to any CRM order.

limitations: The delegated 'windows' source scope was not materialised: the task context reports no platforms and no source scopes, so no Windows registry, event-log, prefetch, amcache, or account-usage evidence exists to corroborate the CRM/payment reconciliation.
All three files share one synthetic creation timestamp (1790594136) and no md5 values, so file integrity and provenance chain cannot be independently verified.

The reconciliation rests on the README's stated rule rather than on processor-side cryptographic or transaction-id linkage; no shared transaction hash exists between the CRM table and the settlement log.
Settlement lines are day-granular only, so settlement-to-order timing cannot be verified beyond the date.
The CRM CSV shows 4 rows and the log 4 lines; absence of further records is only as good as the completeness of these two files.
warnings: The near-identical ids ORD-72033 (settlement) and ORD-70233 (CRM) are a plausible transcription error or deliberate near-miss; do not merge them without an authoritative processor-side correction.
Amount 9999 on the ORD-72033 line is suspiciously round and does not match any CRM amount; treat it as unattributed funds pending follow-up.
No existing analyses or claims were present in the task, so this result introduces the linkage baseline rather than reconciling against prior findings.
